narrative:
The model estimates a 66% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that, in combination, signal a higher risk of departure compared to colleagues who are expected to stay.

The strongest influence comes from the fact that you have received other job opportunities while at your current employer. Unlike most employees predicted to stay—where only about 23% report similar external offers—this stands out as the top factor pushing the prediction toward leaving, as it suggests you have viable alternatives available.

Next, your 11+ years of total professional experience also contributes significantly to the "will leave" outcome. While this level of seniority is relatively uncommon among those expected to remain (only 15% in that group), the model associates longer overall careers with a greater likelihood of moving on to new roles.

Finally, your difficult work-life balance adds further weight toward leaving. This is uncommon among stayers, where the vast majority report medium or easy balance, making your situation another clear driver of the higher risk score.

The organization should consider discussing ways to improve your work-life balance and exploring retention strategies that address external opportunities. You may wish to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your long-term career goals given your extensive experience.
